notice.no_active_file: Clipboard Monitor: open a note to start watch mode
settings.polling.heading: Polling
settings.polling.desc: Obsidian doesn't give plugins a way to be notified when the system clipboard changes, so watch mode checks it on a repeating interval instead. Faster polling notices new clipboard content sooner but uses more CPU; slower polling is lighter but adds a little delay before content is inserted.
settings.polling.tip: Tip: Fast polling paired with "Clear clipboard after image insert" below is a good combination for staying responsive without wasting CPU.
settings.polling.label: Polling frequency
settings.images.heading: Images
settings.images.clear_after_insert.label: Clear clipboard after image insert
settings.images.clear_after_insert.desc: When an image is saved and inserted, clear the entire system clipboard immediately afterward — not just the inserted image, but every format currently on the clipboard (e.g. accompanying text from the same copy is lost too). Re-copying the same image afterward is treated as new content and will be inserted again. Off by default.
settings.formats.heading: Text formats
settings.formats.desc: Templates used to format clipboard text before it's inserted. Use {{content}} for the copied text, {{time}} for the current time, and \n for a new line.
settings.formats.reset_confirm_message: This replaces every text format with the shipped defaults. Your customizations can't be recovered.
settings.debug.heading: Debugging
settings.debug.label: Debug logging
settings.debug.desc: Log watch mode's polling, dedupe, and insertion activity to Obsidian's developer console (View → Toggle Developer Tools → Console), prefixed with "[Clipboard Monitor]". Off by default. Takes effect immediately, even while watch mode is already running.
settings.ribbon.heading: Ribbon icon
settings.ribbon.label: Show ribbon icon
settings.ribbon.desc: Show a clipboard icon in the left ribbon that opens "Start watch mode (choose settings)" when clicked. Takes effect the next time the plugin loads (e.g. after restarting Obsidian or toggling the plugin off and on).
modal.watch.title: Start watch mode
